error_chain: Next.js's webpack-config.ts injects an enhanced-resolve alias for transpilePackages so pnpm-symlinked workspace packages are visible to Webpack's resolver
Turbopack uses its own Rust resolver in turbopack-resolve/resolve.rs with a resolve_options_context that does not honor transpilePackages by default
When pnpm symlinks @internal/ui under apps/<app>/node_modules pointing to .pnpm/<store>/node_modules/@internal/ui, Webpack follows the symlink and loads the package
Turbopack's resolver, lacking the transpilePackages bridge, treats .pnpm-style nested links as outside the workspace root and refuses to load them, raising 'Module not found'
trigger_conditions: The customer uses pnpm with workspaces and consumes a workspace package via transpilePackages in next.config.js
Turbopack does not apply transpilePackages aliases (Next 14 limitation) so the resolver does not bridge the symlinked store
Webpack's enhanced-resolve follows pnpm symlinks transparently while Turbopack's default resolver does not

expected_answer.error_origin: turbopack-resolve/src/resolve.rs not honoring transpilePackages aliases that Next.js's webpack-config.ts applies for workspace packages
expected_answer.bypass_reason: Turbopack's resolve_options_context does not bridge pnpm-symlinked workspace packages the way Webpack's enhanced-resolve does
expected_answer.correct_config: Pin the workspace package via experimental.turbo.resolveAlias in next.config.js, or move the package to a normal dependency until Turbopack adopts transpilePackages parity
